question:

Conclusions:
I. M > D
II. S ≤ M
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
explanation:

II: S ≤ M always holds in the chain, so it follows.
Answer: Only conclusion II follows.

Deepa sits somewhere between Wasim and Farah. Lata sits somewhere between Deepa and Farah. Lata and Wasim are not neighbours. Farah sits at one of the extreme ends.
Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation:
Start with the clues that fix a position (ends, 'immediately left of'), then place the rest.
• Wasim sits somewhere to the left of Lata.
• Exactly one person sits between Farah and Gautam.
• Deepa sits somewhere between Wasim and Farah.
• Lata sits somewhere between Deepa and Farah.
• Lata and Wasim are not neighbours.
• Farah sits at one of the extreme ends.
Only one order satisfies every clue, left to right: Wasim, Deepa, Gautam, Lata, Farah.
Who sits at the extreme left end? Wasim.

II. M ≥ V
options: Either conclusion I or II follows

Both conclusions I and II follow
explanation:
Read the chain V < M = R = W ≤ U from W to R and from M to V. A mix of > and < (or ≥ and ≤) between two letters breaks the link.

question: In a certain code, TABLE is written as VCDNG. How will PLAN be written in that code?
explanation:
Compare TABLE with VCDNG letter by letter: T→V (+2), A→C (+2), B→D (+2), L→N (+2), E→G (+2).

Apply it to PLAN: P→R, L→N, A→C, N→P, giving RNCP.

explanation:
Counting from the top (23) and from the bottom (21) counts this student twice.
